Expectation1: Help out during difficult times or emergencies.
Situation1: You get a frantic call from your friend whose car has broken down on the side of the highway late at night, and they need you to come get them immediately.
Situation2: They fill a high-risk chemotherapy prescription where even a small error could have severe consequences for the patient.
Story: It was nearly midnight when my phone buzzed with a call from Sam, my oldest friend. His voice trembled as he told me his car had broken down on the highway, miles from anywhere, and he needed me to come get him right away. My heart lurched—Sam had always been there for me, and I knew he was counting on me now. But as I glanced at the prescription in my hand, my stomach twisted. I was the only pharmacist on duty, and I was in the middle of preparing a high-risk chemotherapy medication. Every step required my full attention; even the smallest mistake could endanger a patient’s life. I could hear the desperation in Sam’s voice, but I also felt the weight of my professional responsibility pressing down on me. My mind raced, torn between the urgent need to help my friend and the critical duty to my patient. I stood frozen, the phone pressed to my ear, caught between two worlds that both demanded everything from me.
